title: Which Figure Is Settled With the Customer on a Northbeam Renew Trade-In Batch
content:
Which figure is settled follows the revised offers standing on the agreement's trade-in history, since a revised offer put to the customer is the figure the retailer has undertaken to pay. The revised offers looked at are the revised offer entries standing in the Northbeam Renew Trade-In agreement's own trade-in history.

**Where more than one revised offer stands on the agreement's trade-in history**
the amount settled is the highest revised offer standing on it, because the retailer holds to the best offer it has put.

**Where one revised offer stands on the agreement's trade-in history**
the amount settled is that revised offer.

**Where no revised offer stands on the agreement's trade-in history**
the amount settled is the amount the appraisal supports.

**Reading the three branches.** The count of revised offers standing on the history decides which branch governs: two or more, exactly one, or none. Where two or more stand, it is the highest of them that is settled, not the latest; where exactly one stands, that one is settled whether it is higher or lower than the amount the appraisal supports.

**Worked comparison on hypothetical inputs.**

| Revised offers standing on the trade-in history | Amount the appraisal supports | Amount settled |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none | 3200.00 USD | 3200.00 USD |
| one, at 2950.00 USD | 3200.00 USD | 2950.00 USD |
| two, at 2950.00 USD and 3050.00 USD | 3200.00 USD | 3050.00 USD |
| three, at 2950.00 USD, 3400.00 USD and 3100.00 USD | 3200.00 USD | 3400.00 USD |
